Prevention: Store properly dried, non- infested grains (at 12% moisture content) in hermetic bags
Remove previous years grains, debris, contaminants and thoroughly clean the storage facilities
Inspect all grains and storage containers thoroughly before use
Never mix infested with non-infested grains
Dry barley grains in the sun to achieve 13% of moisture content
Before storing new grains, remove infested residues from the previous harvest, sweep floors and inspect walls for holes and cracks to amend
Monitoring: Look out for small (3-5mm long) brownish to blackish adult insects with an elongated snout on stored grains
Check grains for adult emergence holes with irregular edges
Disturb stored grains to check for weevils migrating upwards to the surface
Monitor regularly and thoroughly for weevil reappearance – it may take a while to get rid of them completely
When 5-10 weevils are detected, take action to control them
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Store grains in tightly sealed glass, metal, sturdy plastic containers, or hermetic bags (not normal bags)
Place black pepper around the grain stores to repel weevils
Apply neem seed powder into grain storage at 20g/kg of barley.
Alternatively, finely spray the grains with need oil or neem leaf extract.
Spray the grain in shade and wait for the grains to dry well and put them back into storage.
Coating of wood ash, edible oils or inert clay to prevent further development of the weevils
Sun dry bags of infected grains for 48 hours using either tarpaulin sheets or drying floors
Sieve infested grains and dry again in the sun to kill the remaining eggs and adults
Direct Control (Chemical): When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
Dust dust) at 1kg per tonne (3-6 months under ideal (cool, dry) conditions)
Fumigate stores with phosphine to eliminate existing infestation.
For best results (at ambient temperature), 'under gas' period should be for 8 days, or slightly longer during cold season
Restrictions: Fumifations for stores and storage containers must be done by experts.
